title: Principles of Roman Law
translator: Marguerite Wolff (from the German 'Prinzipien des römischen Rechts', 1934)
subject: Roman law
Legal history
Roman jurisprudence
Methodology of legal science
structure_note: A series of chapters, each devoted to one governing principle of Roman law. The fragment held covers chapter IV, 'Abstraction' (pp. 40-65), on the Roman jurists' reluctance to define, to generalize, and to systematize.

scan.format: PDF with an embedded text layer (OCR of a printed scan)
scan.page_numbering: PDF page 1 corresponds to printed book page 40
scan.quality_note: The embedded text layer is unproof-read OCR: ligatures, Latin and Greek words, italic footnote references and running heads are frequently mangled. Corrections were applied only in the translation, not in text/.

coverage_note: Fragment 1 holds chapter IV ('Abstraction') complete, pp. 40-65, including its footnotes and the bilingual Latin/English reprint of D. 9. 2. 7. 1-8; 9 pr.-4; 11 pr.-5 on pp. 58-62. No other chapter is in the library.

text_extraction.method: pypdf PdfReader.extract_text() over the PDF's own text layer
text_extraction.script: ad hoc; tools/ingest_fragment.py was not used because this PDF already carries a text layer

translations.conventions: Latin and Greek quotations and technical terms are left untranslated in their original form; square brackets inside Latin texts are Schulz's and mark passages he holds spurious. Bibliographic references in the footnotes keep their original form and abbreviations. Printed pagination is marked inline as [с. NN]. Obvious OCR defects in the source text layer were silently corrected against the sense (e.g. 'in hire civili' -> 'in iure civili', 'liber opcov' -> 'liber horon', 'maiores XXV minis' -> 'maiores XXV annis').
